title: Do ciphertext-feedback coefficients decode these pages?
question: Does the pinned three-page short-history coefficient search recover its in-domain plants and produce an English-score hit on LP2?
reader_question: Could earlier ciphertext runes supply the next key?
summary: The source's 60,864 full-page decodes yield no score near its signal bar on LP2-00, LP2-05 or LP2-20. Two additional plants within the default seed grid recover perfectly; two published prose maxima do not match the current pinned executable.
finding: A 5,072-vector, two-seed, two-sign search per page produces best scores -6.90, -6.93 and -6.89 versus the source's -5.2 signal threshold. The source prose reports -6.86/-6.91/-6.89, differing on two pages from the pinned current executable. Its original const5 gate passes but lies outside the const0/const1 search; separate const0 and const1 a1=7 plants rank first among 112 one-tap rules and recover 100% of plaintext. Constant seeds make skips invisible, so these controls do not establish skip recovery.
limitations: Three pages only; third feedback tap limited to five values, constant seeds 0/1, offset zero, one English model and beam width 250. No full-search matched null and no held-out plaintext. Neither these negative scores nor other source rhetoric excludes all feedback methods.
next_steps: Test a new specific feedback rule with a variable-seed plant that truly exercises skips, then evaluate a held-out page and a full-search null under the same selection procedure.

scope.representation: Source GP29 transcription of page ordinals 0, 5 and 20; 262, 263 and 269 rune indices respectively.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged D-04 source full default grid, parse source stdout and independently reconstruct/rescore each winning feedback term. Separately search all 112 one-tap configurations for each of two declared in-domain plants.
scope.parameters: 28 one-tap, 840 two-tap and 4,204 three-tap coefficient vectors; const0/const1 seeds, signs +/-1, offset0, source English-scored beam width250 and max three skips; 60,864 page decodes total.
scope.exclusions: 52 other nonempty pages, const5 and referenced-text seeds in default LP2 grid, other starts/taps/functions, variable-seed skip power and held-out plaintext verification.

review.reviewer: Pinned-source complete-grid stdout, coefficient-count audit, independent winner feedback-term reconstruction and two in-domain planted searches

reproduction.command: python experiments/records/dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients/run.py --source-root SOURCE && python experiments/records/dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients/diagnostic.py --source-root SOURCE --check && python experiments/records/dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients/check.py --source-root SOURCE --check && python experiments/records/dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients/plot.py --check
reproduction.environment: Python 3.9+, NumPy and pinned Dukotah checkout f08b20b. Source program prints its grid result; runner verifies source hashes and captures stdout.

sources.label: Source summary with earlier reported maxima

visuals.caption: In-domain planted controls score above the source signal bar; three searched manuscript pages remain far below it.

reader_finding: None of 60,864 decodes reached the English-score threshold on the three tested pages. The search did recover both planted examples that used its allowed starting values.
reader_limit: Only LP2-00, 05 and 20 were tested, using up to three earlier ciphertext runes and constant starting values 0 or 1. Those constant values cannot reveal whether the decoder handles key skips correctly.
